newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian shares close up ahead of key coalition meet.
newsitem.headline: Indian shares close up ahead of key coalition meet.

text.p: Indian shares ended higher on Thursday as investors awaited the outcome of a key United Front meeting to elect a new leader, traders said.
The alliance said it is due to meet on Friday at 9:30 p.m. (1600 GMT) to discuss replacing caretaker Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda as its leader.
Traders said top banking stock State Bank of India and petrochemicals giant Reliance Industries led the uptrend.
"The general mood is optimistic," said a chief dealer at a local brokerage. "People are hopeful of the budget going through."
Shares of India's largest private firm Reliance surged 12.0 rupees, or 4.5 percent, to close at 280.
Traders said speculators were bidders ahead of the company's results for the financial year ended March 31, 1997 which are due on April 22.
"We have given greater autonomy to banks to determine working capital limits for borrowers and also eased norms on consortium lending," he said.
Shares of top commercial bank State Bank of India climbed 9.50 rupees, or 3.3 percent, to close at 296 in large volumes.

"The policy doesn't add directly to banks' bottomlines but the fact that they have been given much more operational freedom is a big plus point, especially for the frontline banks," said a banking analyst at a foreign brokerage.
"It was an excellent policy and is bound to make liquidity easier," said a fund manager.
"If only the politics would sort itself out you could really see the market running. We need to get the political issue out of the way," he added.
In Delhi, shares closed higher in hectic trade as investors bought on expectations that the political impasse would be resolved soon, traders said.
The Delhi Stock Exchange's sensitive index closed 9.16 points higher at 769.88.
Most exchanges across the country except in Madras will remain closed on Friday due to a Moslem holiday.
